title: The list edge-coloring conjecture
formal: Does every finite loopless multigraph have list chromatic index equal to its chromatic index?
context:
List chromatic index is the least k guaranteeing an edge coloring for every assignment of lists of k colors. Bipartite multigraphs are a solved special case.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks whether arbitrary local restrictions on allowed edge colors impose any additional global cost.
